title: Closing The Visibility Gap
gist: Gregory Haley argues that no single test, inspection, model or on-chip monitor sees all of an advanced device. The bottleneck has shifted from collecting more data to connecting wafer, test, manufacturing-history and field data with context. Vendors including Teradyne, proteanTecs, Synopsys, Siemens EDA, ZEISS and Nordson describe specific blind spots in advanced packaging.

insights.claim: Voids, solder cracks and head-in-pillow defects in advanced-package interconnects often pass electrical test because physical contact exists, yet cause premature field failure.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Electrical test alone underestimates reliability risk in advanced packaging, which supports demand for X-ray/inspection tools.
insights.quote: Voids, cracks in the solder, and head-in-pillow are a few predominant defect types that pass electrical test due to the presence of physical contact. But these defects usually lead to premature failure.

insights.claim: Gaps remain in pull testing for copper pillars and RDL integrity, and X-ray still struggles with overlays of wires and bumps in stacked dies and tiny TSV features, with trade-offs between power, throughput and resolution.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Unsolved inspection gaps in 3D stacking are an opportunity for metrology/inspection innovators.
insights.quote: Users also have to make choices between power, throughput, and resolution.
insights.locator: For testing, there is a gap

insights.claim: Brute-force high-resolution X-ray scanning is impractical because it is slow and generates gigabytes to terabytes of data, so heuristics are needed to decide where to look.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Value is shifting toward smart targeting and analytics layered on top of inspection hardware.
insights.quote: It’s really not practical to just do a brute-force high-resolution X-ray scan, because high resolution means small pixels, means it’s slow

insights.claim: Failure analysis works as progressive narrowing: electrical test finds the neighborhood, acoustic/optical narrows it, X-ray looks inside non-destructively, and electron microscopy with cross-sectioning confirms the mechanism.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: A multi-tool flow means FA labs buy across modalities, and the tools complement one another.

insights.claim: Wafer-scale macro inspection acts as an 'eye in the sky' screen that coexists with high-resolution micro tools rather than replacing them.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Low-cost macro screening tools keep a role even as nodes advance.
insights.quote: It’s your eye in the sky. It sees everything from a higher level, but you don’t stop there.
insights.locator: If you’re struggling with a problem

themes.theme: Evidence already exists but is disconnected

insights.claim: Test escapes are often not caused by missing measurements; the signal may already be sitting in wafer data, equipment telemetry, manufacturing history or field data spread across disconnected groups.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Data integration and traceability software, not more sensors, is the leverage point for yield and quality.
insights.quote: Test escapes aren’t always caused because we have missing measurements

insights.claim: Retained historical inspection images let engineers trace a late-line thermal wafer breakage back to a tiny early edge deformation, and negative evidence (where a mark first disappears going backward) pinpoints the origin step.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Image retention and traceability carry more value than their storage cost suggests.
insights.quote: One of the keys is just having the historical images
insights.locator: One of the keys is just

insights.claim: Anomalies are most often overlooked when the trend looks positive, such as higher yield or lower test time, even though unexplained improvements still carry information.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Unexplained good news in yield data can hide risk; analytics should flag unexplained shifts in both directions.
insights.quote: If the anomaly produces lower test time or higher yield, it is more likely to be overlooked.

insights.claim: Teradyne's Roth argues the answer is not more data or bigger, smarter models but connected data and ecosystems that link wafer sort, final test, SLT, manufacturing history and field performance in closed feedback loops.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Favors vendors of cross-insertion data platforms and closed-loop analytics over standalone AI models.
insights.quote: I don’t think the answer is going to be building bigger, giant, smarter, more capable models.
insights.locator: How can we connect wafer sort

insights.claim: A statistical model can be statistically correct yet operationally wrong because it is missing context, such as clues held in an earlier insertion or manufacturing history.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Shows a limit of ML-only test analytics and the need for context-rich data pipelines.
insights.quote: A model could be statistically correct, but it could still be operationally incorrect

insights.claim: Socket contact-resistance variability from wear, contamination and repeated insertions can create enough noise to hide real failure signatures, yet test data usually assumes the interconnect is good.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Test-cell hardware health matters to data quality, which creates demand for socket monitoring and maintenance.

insights.claim: Customers demand silicon correlation data before trusting EDA thermal simulation, and correlation quality keeps improving, but accurate comparison with embedded sensors requires assembling die, package and PCB in the same stack-up.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Multiphysics system-level simulation is becoming a requirement, which benefits EDA vendors with integrated 3D-IC flows.
insights.quote: You cannot just do the single-die simulation or single-package simulation or single PCB
insights.locator: You cannot just do the single-die

insights.claim: Advanced packaging makes material properties such as thermal conductivity and Young's modulus harder to characterize, so values do not transfer cleanly between packages.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Material characterization becomes a bottleneck for simulation accuracy in 2.5D/3D designs.
insights.quote: Advanced packaging makes some of the underlying physical properties, such as thermal conductivity or Young’s modulus, much harder to characterize

insights.claim: A package can meet its average temperature target while local regions run substantially hotter, and in 2.5D/3D packages workloads move hotspots across neighboring dies.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Averages understate thermal reliability risk in AI chips, so dense distributed thermal sensing gains value.
insights.quote: Average temperature often hides the conditions that drive reliability concerns

insights.claim: Classical analog thermal sensors sit at chip edges because they are large and need analog supply, which is no longer sufficient; temperature must be probed at many hotspot locations.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Supports demand for compact distributed on-chip monitoring IP such as proteanTecs.
insights.quote: with the chips of today that’s no longer sufficient

insights.claim: Even dense on-chip monitoring cannot observe inside SRAM; inputs and outputs are visible, but a write error may only surface when data is read later.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Memory remains an observability blind spot, which leaves an opening for new reliability IP.
insights.quote: We don’t know what’s happening inside the memory.

insights.claim: Test and monitoring are complementary: test establishes time-zero quality, while in-field monitoring is needed to ensure reliability over the chip's useful life.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Lifecycle monitoring is an additive market, not a substitute for ATE spend.
insights.quote: You cannot avoid test by having monitoring

insights.claim: Synopsys says the gap between modeled and measured behavior is closing and is already much better than before.
insights.speaker: Gregory Haley
insights.so_what: Better simulation-silicon correlation increases the value of digital-twin and simulation tooling.
